If system\n243\t/// time is unavailable or chrono formatting fails (e.g., due to extreme\n244\t/// system clock values that overflow chrono's internal calculations), it\n245\t/// falls back to the Unix epoch timestamp (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and\n246\t/// logs an error message to stderr.\n247\t///\n248\t/// # Returns\n249\t///\n250\t/// * `String` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or the epoch\n251\t///   timestamp as a fallback if time capture fails\n252\t///\n253\t/// # Fallback Behavior\n254\t///\n255\t/// When the system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n256\t/// or chrono formatting fails, this function:\n257\t/// - Returns `\"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\"` (Unix epoch)\n258\t/// - Logs an error message to stderr with failure details\n259\t/// - Never panics, ensuring the function is safe to call in production\n260\t///\n261\t/// # Examples\n262\t///\n263\t/// ```no_run\n264\t/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp;\n265\t///\n266\t/// let now = capture_timestamp();\n267\t/// println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", now);\n268\t/// // Output: \"2026-08-13T14:30:00Z\" (or epoch on failure)\n269\t/// ```\n270\t///\n271\t/// # Performance\n272\t///\n273\t/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n274\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n275\t///\n276\t/// # Error Handling\n277\t///\n278\t/// For use cases that need to distinguish between success and failure,\n279\t/// use [`capture_timestamp_result()`] instead, which returns a `Result`.\n280\tpub fn capture_timestamp() -> String {\n281\t    capture_timestamp_result().unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n282\t        eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}. Using epoch fallback.\", e);\n283\t        // Unix epoch as ISO 8601 timestamp (fallback when system time fails)\n284\t        \"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\".to_string()\n285\t    })\n286\t}\n287\t\n288\t/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n289\t///\n290\t/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n291\t/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n292\t///\n293\t/// This is the fallible version of [`capture_timestamp()`] that returns\n294\t/// a `Result` instead of handling errors internally. 8601 format, or an\n300\t///   error if time capture fails\n301\t///\n302\t/// # Errors\n303\t///\n304\t/// This function returns an error if:\n305\t/// - The system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n306\t/// - Chrono formatting fails to produce an ISO 8601 string (e.g., due to\n307\t///   extreme system clock values)\n308\t///\n309\t/// # Examples\n310\t///\n311\t/// call to get the current time and should\n323\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n324\tpub fn capture_timestamp_result() -> Result<String> {\n325\t    // Use catch_unwind to handle any potential panics from chrono operations\n326\t    // This protects against extreme edge cases like system clock overflow\n327\t    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n328\t        let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n329\t        now.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)\n330\t    }));\n331\t\n332\t    match result {\n333\t        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n334\t        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n335\t            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n336\t        )),\n337\t    }\n338\t}\n339\t\n340\t/// Parse the backend name from a binary's version output.\n341\t///\n342\t/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\n343\t/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\n344\t///\n345\t/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\n346\t/// the binary to execute\n352\t/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\"--version\"]`)\n353\t///\n354\t/// # Returns\n355\t///\n356\t/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\n357\t///   - Binary not found\n358\t///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\n359\t///   - Output is empty or unparseable\n360\t///\n361\t/// # Examples\n362\t///\n363\t/// ```no_run\n364\t/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\n365\t/// use std::path::Path;\n366\t///\n367\t/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n368\t/// let std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n381\t    use std::thread;\n382\t\n383\t    // Check if binary exists\n384\t    if !binary_path.exists() {\n385\t        anyhow::bail!(\"binary not found at {}\", binary_path.display());\n386\t    }\n387\t\n388\t    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \"Text file busy\"\n389\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n390\t    let     .args(version_args)\n397\t            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n398\t            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n399\t            .output();\n400\t\n401\t        match result {\n402\t            Ok(output) => {\n403\t                if attempt > 0 {\n404\t                    debug!(\n405\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n406\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n407\t                        binary = %binary_path.display(),\n408\t                        function = \"parse_backend_name_from_version\",\n409\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n410\t                        attempt + 1\n411\t                    );\n412\t                }\n413\t\n414\t                // Check exit status\n415\t                if         );\n423\t                }\n424\t\n425\t                // Capture stdout\n426\t                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n427\t                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\n428\t\n429\t                // Extract backend name (first word)\n430\t                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\n431\t             })?;\n436\t\n437\t                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\n438\t            }\n439\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n440\t                last_err = Some(e);\n441\t                warn!(\n442\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n443\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n444\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n445\t                    binary = %binary_path.display(),\n446\t                    function = \"parse_backend_name_from_version\",\n447\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n448\t                    attempt + 1,\n449\t                    max_attempts,\n450\t                    backoff_ms\n451\t                );\n452\t                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n453\t            }\n454\t            Err(e) => {\n455\t                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\n456\t                    format!(\n457\t                        \"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\",\n458\t                        binary_path.display(),\n459\t                        version_args\n460\t                    )\n461\t                })\n462\t            }\n463\t        }\n464\t    }\n465\t\n466\t    // All retries exhausted\n467\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\")).with_context(\n468\t        || {\n469\t            format!(\n470\t                \"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\",\n471\t                binary_path.display(),\n472\t                max_attempts\n473\t            )\n474\t        },\n475\t    )\n476\t}\n477\t\n478\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n479\t///\n480\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n481\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n482\t/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n483\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n484\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n485\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n486\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n487\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n488\t///\n489\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n490\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n491\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n492\t#[cfg(test)]\n493\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\n494\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\n495\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n496\t\n497\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n498\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n499\t\n500\t    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\n501\t    ///\n502\t    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\n503\t    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\n504\t    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\n505\t    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\n506\t    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\n507\t    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\n508\t    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\n509\t        \"HOME\",\n510\t        \"PATH\",\n511\t        \"NEEDLE_HOME\",\n512\t        \"NEEDLE_EVENTS\",\n513\t        \"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\",\n514\t    ];\n515\t\n516\t    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\n517\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n518\t        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\n519\t    }\n520\t\n521\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n522\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\n523\t            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\n524\t                restore(key, value);\n525\t            }\n526\t        }\n527\t    }\n528\t\n529\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n530\t        match value {\n531\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n532\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n533\t        }\n534\t    }\n535\t\n536\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n537\t    ///\n538\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n539\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n540\t    /// registry. let lock = ENV_LOCK\n571\t            .lock()\n572\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n573\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\n574\t            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n575\t                .iter()\n576\t                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n577\t                .collect(),\n578\t        };\n579\t        (lock, guard)\n580\t    }\n581\t}\n582\t\n583\t#[cfg(test)]\n584\tmod tests {\n585\t    use super::*;\n586\t    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\n587\t    use std::env;\n588\t    use std::path::PathBuf;\n589\t\n590\t
